text:
Mattias Ekholm is the steadiest part of one of the most fortunate teams in hockey. Edmonton has scored 17.6 more goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice, the kind of number that comes from playing behind Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl while both are finishing at absurd rates. His own line is nine points in 17 games and a four-game point streak, and the Oilers take 53% of the expected goals at five on five with him out there.

The process is real. Evolving-Hockey had him driving play last season, +0.29 expected goals per 60 for his team once teammates and competition are accounted for, 98th percentile among defencemen. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him getting to the slot more than almost any defenceman and breaking the puck out cleanly 54% of the time. What won't hold is the luck around him. When the Oilers' shooting cools, his plus numbers will shrink, and that will say nothing about how well he's playing. At 36, the thing to watch is his minutes: down 1:15 a night over the last ten games.
